protected_scheduled_posts.hook: Spot the herd.
Giant pandas spend about half of every day eating bamboo.
Many flowers carry ultraviolet patterns we can't see, which guide bees straight to the nectar.
A group of cats is called a clowder.
Ferns are older than the dinosaurs. They first appeared more than 350 million years ago.
In Japan, the cherry blossom forecast is tracked across the country like the weather.
Bees see ultraviolet light, so to them a daisy looks like a target pointing to its center.
Cats have about 50 vertebrae in their spine. We have 33. That's how they stretch like this.
A chickadee can remember thousands of spots where it hid seeds for winter.
Twilight comes in three stages: civil, nautical and astronomical. Each one is a little darker.
Moonflowers open at dusk and close by morning. Night moths do the pollinating.
Cats can see in about one sixth of the light we need.
One theory says monstera leaves split as they grow to let wind and light through to the leaves below.
A honeybee beats its wings about 200 times a second. That's the buzz.
The evening star isn't a star at all. It's Venus.
A cat's whiskers are about as wide as its body, so they work like a built in measuring tape.
Most coastlines get two high tides a day, and every one refills the tide pools.
Hanami, the tradition of picnicking under cherry blossoms, goes back more than a thousand years.
Daisies grow on every continent except Antarctica.
A 2019 study found that 20 minutes in nature was enough to lower stress hormone levels.
Cats have a third eyelid that sweeps across the eye to keep it clean.
Koi can live for decades, and some have been recorded living past 100 years.
Cats can turn their ears 180 degrees, using more than 30 muscles in each ear.
On a clear, dark night you can see a few thousand stars without a telescope.
In its whole life, one honeybee makes about a twelfth of a teaspoon of honey.
Adult cats rarely meow at each other. They save it for talking to us.
